exposure: Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR) as PE diagnostic criterion
Maternal organ dysfunction as PE diagnostic criterion
outcome: Maternal morbidities (severe hypertension, need for intravenous antihypertensives, magnesium sulfate, composite of major maternal complications)
cohort: The study included singleton pregnancies diagnosed with preeclampsia, categorized into those with FGR without maternal organ dysfunction (Group F) and those with maternal organ dysfunction without FGR (Group M) at diagnosis.
finding: The presence of FGR on PE diagnosis is associated with an earlier diagnosis and delivery, and leads to severe maternal symptoms comparable to those caused by maternal organ dysfunction at diagnosis.
gest_age: PE diagnosis before 34 weeks of gestation was a specific subgroup analyzed, and diagnosis/delivery times were reported in weeks of gestation.
